text:
sam: Heads-up — prod tps/tokens/sec fell ~22% after the canary rolled at ~3567894200. Started seeing token/sec sink and longer enqueue waits. filing this here before I dig deeper.

maria: ugh. noticed higher p99 latency on customer routes too. Is this the scheduler change from last merge? @alex do you know the rollout tag? :eyes:

alex: that was the 'adaptive-admission' refactor, merged in #4432 yesterday. deploys to canary then prod. I put rollout hold on further canaries for now.

jordan: perf-bot flagged a regression on nightly perf suite: `inference_throughput_test` down 18% on xlarge. CI link: https://ci.internal/runs/98812 (perf-bot posted numbers).

perf-bot: DETECTED: throughput regression in inference_throughput_test (baseline 1250 tok/s -> 1025 tok/s). Suspected area: scheduler/admission.

lee: quick profiling on staging shows a pattern: many more tiny batches (1-3 examples) and memcpy spikes in kernel path. KV cache miss-rate up ~3x for recent requests.

pat: paste of the flame snippet and a short log (staging):
```
enqueue_latency_ms: median=45 -> 320, p95=210 -> 980
batch_sizes: median=8 -> 2, small_batch_count++
memcpy_cnt(kernel): 2.2M -> 5.9M
kv_cache_hits: 78% -> 26%
```

sam: interesting — admission refactor added per-worker fairness tokens. hypothesis: skewed token bucket/aging causes some worker threads to starve, so continuous-batcher coalesces fewer requests -> lots of small batches -> increased kernel memcpy and kv thrash.

maria: can we reproduce locally with traffic replay? I can run replay under the merged binary. what commit range to bisect?

alex: start bisection between `main@f1a2c` (pre-refactor) and `main@d9b4e` (post-refactor merge). PR #4432 is `d9b4e`.

jordan: suggestion: run the perf harness with `--enable-ctb --trace-enqueue` and collect `kv_hit_ratio` metric. command I used locally:
```
./perf_harness --workload=chat_realtime --concurrency=64 --duration=300 --enable-ctb --trace-enqueue > run.log
```

pat: running that on staging now. initial output shows `avg_tok_per_sec=1040` (vs baseline 1320). attaching short excerpt:
```
[run] 00:01:30 tokens/s=1103 enq_ms=270 batch_med=3 kv_hit=31%
[run] 00:03:00 tokens/s=1021 enq_ms=310 batch_med=2 kv_hit=28%
```

lee: low-hanging mitigation: revert admission back to previous weights or disable per-worker aging. I'm fine with a quick revert to restore throughput while we bisect.

maria: agreed. is there a hotfix PR? alex?

alex: opened revert PR #4440 that restores previous admission loop. CI is running. If CI green, we can roll back canary and prod.

ci-bot: CI: test-suite passed; perf-checker reported NO significant regression for revert branch. Perf-check: inference_throughput_test diff +1.2% (within noise).

sam: okay planning to roll revert to canary in 10m. but we should still bisect to understand root cause. I don't want to hide a deeper scheduling bug.

jordan: for bisect plan: run binary slices with perf harness focusing on two signals: `enqueue_latency_ms` and `kv_hit_ratio`. Also capture `kernel_memcpy_ops` from perf counters. If we see steady kv_hit drop coincident with small-batch spike we can tie to admission behavior.

pat: running quick bisect job starting at 3567894520 (pre) -> 3567894600 (post) with 6 steps. will post results to thread.

perf-bot: TIP: add `--batch-stat-log` to capture per-second batch distribution histogram. that helped earlier investigations.

lee: one more data point: I dumped scheduler metrics on the problematic binary and saw sustained `worker_idle_ratio` variance: some workers at 2% idle, others at 65% — that imbalance looks like admission tokens are not being shared correctly across worker groups.

maria: thanks. after revert lands and canary looks healthy we should still run an extended test (2h) with traffic replay and `kv_hotset` skew to stress-cache effects.

alex: rolling back canary now. will monitor metrics.

sam: update 3567894365 — reverted canary -> prod token/sec recovered to ~baseline within two deploy cycles. keeping rollout hold on the admission refactor until post-mortem and fix.

maria: assigning follow-up: bisect results, scheduler unit tests to cover worker-token sharing, perf regression test added to PR checklist. I'll create an RFC for safer admission changes.

jordan: leaving notes for the postmortem: include flamegraphs, batch histograms, kv hit-rate timelines, and the bisect commit that caused the change.

pat: posted bisect raw outputs to the eng-runtime drive: https://internal.drive/r/ctb-bisect-3567894321

alex: TY everyone. great fast response. :thumbsup:

sam: we should also add an automated guard in canary pipeline: if tokens/sec drops >10% for 10m, auto-hold rollout. filing issue #987.

perf-bot: ACTIONS: created ticket perf-987 (canary throughput guard) and linked PR #4440 (revert).
